title: Classroom & Lecture Hall
summary: The instructor wears the wireless portable transmitter while students seated throughout large lecture auditoriums receive crystal-clear audio through personal receivers, without requiring direct line-of-sight.
why: Non-line-of-sight (NLOS) RF signal penetrates desks, pillars, lecture stands, and physical room obstacles.
Omni-directional broadcast coverage ensures uniform signal strength across a 360-degree radius for all seated students.
Allows the lecturer to move freely around the hall and write on whiteboards without audio dropouts.
cautions: Susceptible to electromagnetic interference from nearby unshielded switched-mode power supplies and heavy electrical machinery.
Signals can penetrate partition walls into adjacent classrooms if RF carrier frequencies are not isolated.

title: Hospital & MRI / Imaging Room
summary: Medical staff and hearing-assisted patients communicate safely inside diagnostic imaging suites, MRI chambers, and ICU wards where radio frequency electromagnetic emissions are strictly prohibited.
why: Zero electromagnetic emissions (0.00% EMI/RFI radiation), guaranteeing no distortion or interference with sensitive MRI coils or telemetry monitors.
Inherent spatial security: optical infrared light cannot penetrate walls, preventing accidental eavesdropping or clinical data leakage.
Immune to heavy RF static generated by high-power medical equipment and motors.
cautions: Strictly requires an unobstructed line-of-sight (LOS) light path between transmitter IR emitter and receiver photodiode.
Direct sunlight or high-intensity unfiltered incandescent medical surgical lamps can saturate the photodiode front-end.

title: Museum & Historic Gallery Tour
summary: Adaptive dual-link system providing broad-range RF coverage in spacious open exhibition halls, seamlessly complementing directed optical light beams at localized display showcases.
why: Total spatial flexibility: broad RF carrier covers main group walking routes, while pinpoint IR optical beams deliver private exhibit audio at individual display cases.
Redundant dual-path capability ensures seamless fallback if one transmission link experiences physical blockage or local noise.
Supports future automated RSSI/Lux sensor-driven switching without manual user intervention.
cautions: Requires dual-channel receiver circuitry on user headsets, slightly increasing battery consumption when both front-ends are active.
Transition zones between open halls and enclosed galleries require balanced receiver sensitivity calibration.
